### When `-exportArchive` fails Two failures land on the same step and have nothing to do with each other. `productbuild failed` with `CSSMERR_CSP_USER_CANCELED` in the distribution log is the keychain: the Mac Installer identity lives in `reachy-signing.keychain-db`, and macOS put up an access dialog that a non-interactive run cannot answer — it "cancels" itself after a few minutes. Authorize the key once and the keychain keeps it: ```bash KC=~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db PW="$(cat ~/.config/reachy-mini/signing/keychain.pw)" security unlock-keychain -p "$PW" "$KC" security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$PW" "$KC" ``` `Failed to Use Accounts` is the Xcode account instead, and only the upload leg needs one. Export locally and hand the artifact to the API key, which does the upload, the group and the Beta App Review submission in one call: ```bash mise run asc -- publish testflight --app 6799644194 --platform IOS \ --ipa "Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/Hey Reachy.ipa" \ --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e \ --wait --test-notes "…" --locale en-US --submit --confirm ``` A macOS `.pkg` is not a zip, so `asc` cannot read the version out of it: that one also needs `--version` and `--build-number` (the commit count) spelled out. ## The store listing The App Store copy lives in this repository, at `metadata/` — `app-info/en-US.json` for the fields that belong to the app (name, subtitle, privacy policy URL) and `version//en-US.json` for the ones that belong to a version (description, keywords, promotional text, support and marketing URLs). Edit those, then: ```bash mise run asc -- metadata validate --dir ./metadata mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata --dry-run mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata ``` Push once per platform — `IOS` and `MAC_OS` carry separate version localizations off the same files. `whatsNew` is deliberately absent: Apple refuses it on an app's **first** App Store version (`Attribute 'whatsNew' cannot be edited at this time`), so release notes start with the second one. Everything that is not a localization is set once and stays: category, content rights, age rating, availability, price, and the reviewer contact and notes. They are listed by `asc validate --app 6799644194 --version-id --platform

`, which is the one command worth running before every submission — it prints an ordered remediation plan and exits non-zero while anything is missing. Two of those answers are judgement calls, and both were decided against the two Reachy apps already on the store rather than from first principles. Pollen's own `Reachy Mini` (id 6766823749) sells the same community app catalogue this one does — "browse and launch community apps instantly" — and stands at **9+** with _Infrequent/Mild Cartoon or Fantasy Violence_ and _Mature/Suggestive Themes_, which is a statement about what a community app might do rather than about the app's own content. The independent `Reachy's Brain` (id 6757115923) is **4+** with no advisories, but it ships no catalogue at all, so it is not the precedent to copy. Hence: `USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT`, because the Apps tab renders a Hugging Face catalogue this project does not own, and every age-rating answer left at `NONE` with an explicit `--age-rating-override-v2 NINE_PLUS` on top — declaring a shelf position rather than asserting content the app does not contain. Both are one `asc` command to revert. Their public halves are readable without a session: `curl -s "https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id="` carries `contentAdvisoryRating`, `advisories` and `genres`; the content-rights declaration is private and cannot be checked this way. ## The public beta `https://testflight.apple.com/join/CGjefT9a` — the **Public Beta** group, `c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e`, capped at 500 testers. The link is in the README; raising the cap is one `groups edit --public-link-limit`, lowering it below the people who already joined is not. Uploading is not distributing. An upload reaches the internal group by itself, because `Internal` carries `hasAccessToAllBuilds`; the public group has to be attached per build, per platform, and each one is its own Beta App Review: ```bash mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform IOS \ --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform MAC_OS \ --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm mise run asc -- testflight review submissions list --build-id "" ``` What review reads lives at the app level, not the build level, so it is written once and stays: the tester-facing text in `testflight app-localizations` (description, feedback email, marketing URL, and the privacy policy at `docs/privacy.md` — which has to resolve on `main`, or review fails on a 404), and the reviewer-facing contact and notes in `testflight review edit`. The notes carry the thing no reviewer can guess — that the app needs a robot nobody at Apple has, that the Bluetooth sheet auto-presenting on first launch hides the Local Network alert underneath it, and that Hugging Face sign-in is the one path that completes without hardware. Beta App Review has no demo account to give, because the app has no accounts. Testers see the same What to Test note per build: ```bash mise run asc -- builds test-notes create --build-id "" \ --locale en-US --whats-new "..." ``` ## Querying App Store Connect `mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded — `Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift. Everything after `--` goes to `asc`: ```bash mise run asc -- apps list mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194 # did the TestFlight upload land? mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194 ``` `asc` resolves a stored profile before the environment, so an `asc auth login` run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status` prints which of the two is answering. The key is App Manager, not Admin, so the same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it cannot manage provisioning profiles. The CLI also ships 23 agent skills (`asc install-skills`, pinned to a reviewed commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing. ## Xcode Cloud (optional, continuous TestFlight) `Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` makes a generated project buildable on Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise` bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot scheme there) are commented at the top of the script.

feat: conversation controls, presence, and phone-recorded moves (#88)

* feat(robot): show how long the robot takes to answer

The status poll already ran every three seconds and threw its duration away.
It now lands in `RobotSession.lastRoundTrip` and beside "Connected" on the
Robot tab, coloured by `HealthLevel.roundTrip`.

Not seeded from the handshake, which reads the same route through a different
call, and cleared by a failed poll: a stale figure next to an unreachable
robot is a lie about the present.

* feat(apps): pin the apps you actually use to the top of the store

A pin lifts a row above the daemon's own ordering; it never filters, so a
search that excludes a pinned app still excludes it. Three ways in: a leading
swipe, a context menu, and Start in that same menu for an app that can take it.

Stored per robot by `RobotIdentity.deduplicationKey` (rule 4), keyed by
`RobotApp.id`. A card pinned in Discover and its installed row are therefore
two keys wherever the Space slug differs from the Python entry point — the pin
reads as lost on install, and re-pinning is one tap.

`canStart` repeats every condition `AppDetailSheet` renders as a banner: a
menu has nowhere to put the sentence that would explain a refusal.

* docs(daemon): record that the media toggles are write-only

`media/wobbling` and `media/tracking` have no route that reports whether
either is on — `media/status` describes the media server, and a face target's
`detected: false` cannot tell "tracking off" from "nobody there".

And wobbling is audio-reactive rather than idle motion: it moves the head under
audio the daemon is playing, so a silent robot with it enabled does not move.
`wobbling/enable` answers ok even when it did nothing, because the call sits
inside a nil check the return is outside of.

* feat(apps): mute the robot and stop it mid-sentence from the dock

`ConversationRPCClient` grows a request half — the twelve methods Conversation
App 1.0 serves were reachable and none was called. The dock now offers two of
them: mute the robot's own microphone, and interrupt it while it is speaking.

One socket per call rather than a multiplexed one. JSON-RPC matches a reply to
its request by id, which on a shared socket means a waiter table, a reconnect
policy that survives a call in flight, and an actor holding both — against a
handshake to a robot on the same network, for a button pressed now and then.

The mute state is remembered, not read: `conversation.mic` is a command and
`conversation.status` answers with backend config. An app that never had these
methods answers -32601, and the controls go rather than reporting a failure
nobody can act on. Restart gives way while a conversation is live, the trade
`inlineRow` already documents.

* feat(live): reach the robot's audio and presence without leaving the stream

The speaker, the microphone and the two daemon-side behaviours are now a sheet
from the viewport rather than a trip to the Settings tab — every one of them is
something you want while looking through the camera, and reaching them used to
=== 87 ===
feat(apps): filter the store by scope and sort it six ways (#87)

A toolbar menu with two inline pickers: a scope (all, official,
community, private) and an order (recommended, name, author, likes,
newest, recently updated).

Scopes are questions rather than buckets, so a private community Space
answers both `.community` and `.privateSpaces` — partitioning them would
hide it from a reader who asked for community apps. Official can only
ever mean the author: there is no verified flag on a Space, and
`_build_app_info` stamps `source_kind = hf_space` on the curated
`app-list.json` list and on the full Spaces list alike.

`.recommended` is the default for the same reason. The daemon puts the
curated entries first and nothing else in the payload records that, so
re-ordering by default would throw away the only editorial signal the
store has.

The two dates were already on the robot and undecoded: `extra.createdAt`
and `extra.lastModified`, folded onto that one spelling by the daemon's
`_normalize_space_data` and present in both of its catalogue paths.
`JSONCodec.daemon` already reads ISO 8601 with fractional seconds, so
they cost two properties and no new parsing.

Every sort ends in a tie-break on title and then id — `sorted(by:)` is
not stable, and without it two apps by the same author swap places
between redraws of a list nobody touched.
=== 86 ===
feat(intents): answer "is Reachy awake" and "what is running" (#86)

* feat(intents): answer "is Reachy awake" and "what is running"

Every intent so far was a command. These two answer a question, entirely
out of the App Group snapshot — no socket, no timeout budget, and nothing
that can fail on an unreachable robot.

The rule they exist to enforce: `isAwake` is false for a parked robot *and*
for a torn-down backend, and those take opposite sequences to undo. A tile
may gloss that as "Asleep" because the word sits beside a wake button that
resolves both meanings itself; a spoken sentence is the whole answer
somebody gets, so `RobotStatusReport` says "not awake" and names both.
A reading past its window reports when it last answered rather than
anything about the present.

`freshReading(for:)` is deliberately not used — it collapses stale and
wrong-robot into one nil, which is right for a caller about to command a
robot and wrong for one about to describe it.

Sentences stay a `LocalizedStringResource` until `IntentDialog` takes one:
flattening to `String` first would put the finished sentence through format
substitution twice, and a robot's name is free text somebody typed.

`ReachyShortcuts` is now at ten of ten, its ceiling.

The speaker, the microphone and the two daemon-side behaviours are now a sheet
from the viewport rather than a trip to the Settings tab — every one of them is
something you want while looking through the camera, and reaching them used to
cost the picture. `AudioSettingsSection` is reused whole.

`media/wobbling` and `media/tracking` were in the spec and called from nowhere.
Wobbling is audio-reactive, not idle motion: it moves the head under audio the
daemon plays, which for this app means the microphone telepresence already
sends. Tracking's reply is honest and reported — a camera-less robot answers
`enabled: false` under a 200, and the switch springs back saying so.

Neither can be read back, so the section says in words that it shows what this
app last asked for. `PresenceClient` is the capability gate, the shape
`CacheMaintenanceClient` has: over the relay the section is absent rather than
inert.

* fix(live): move the hearing badge out of the control row

It is a reading, not a control, and the top row could not hold it: the caption
is a sentence rather than a glyph — deliberately, since the robot's left falls
on opposite sides of the screen in the two viewports and only a word is
unambiguous — so on a phone it wrapped to two lines and took a third of the row.

Bottom leading is the one corner neither viewport claims; `CameraViewport` puts
the joystick and the recentre button in bottom trailing.

Eight references moved and no others: the four of `Viewport — heard a voice`,
and the four of `Apps — pinned`, which the filter menu merged from main puts a
toolbar item on.

* feat(moves): record a move from the phone and play it back

The one thing neither competitor does from the phone itself. Pollen's answer is
an app on the robot (The Marionette) and Reachy's Brain runs a server there;
both put the recording where the robot can lose it, and both need something
installed. A take here is the `TeleopTarget`s `TeleopDriver` already emits, so
playback is the same wire path as driving and works on a bare robot.

Recording lives on the Controller screen, because that is where the targets come
from; the takes play back from the Moves tab, above the robot's own libraries.
Frames carry offsets rather than an assumed rate — the sampler is a main-actor
task and a loaded phone drops ticks, so a take replayed at a nominal 10 Hz would
not be the take that was made.

Not a daemon move: it never appears in `GET /api/move/running`, so playback
frees the move slot first or `play_move` would drop one of the two in silence.
`TeleopTarget` gains `Codable`, which puts its property names inside
`JSONCodec.stored`'s frozen format.

`Moves — dances loading` moved again for no reason belonging to this change —
the unstable spinner CLAUDE.md records — and was restored rather than kept.

* feat(ble): read what a robot advertises before anything connects

The scanner already received the whole advertisement and kept only the local
name — which is identical on every Reachy Mini, so a scan could list three
robots and say nothing about which is which. `BLEPeripheralSnapshot` now carries
`kCBAdvDataManufacturerData` verbatim, and `BLEAdvertisement` decodes the shape
upstream's PR #1086 describes: a hotspot flag, an IPv4 address and seven bytes of
the hardware id under company `0xFFFF`.

No robot here has been seen sending it, so the raw bytes are kept beside the
decoded value and the recovery console prints them as hex — this is how the
question gets answered rather than assumed. A robot on older firmware carries
nil and every screen behaves exactly as before.

The prefix is seven of the hardware id's bytes, not a `deduplicationKey`: the
name says so because a `==` against a stored key would silently never match.

* fix(ble): stop losing the manufacturer block between sightings

Two things were dropping it, and either alone made a robot that advertises look
exactly like one that does not.

`merging` replaced the snapshot wholesale, and CoreBluetooth calls back per
packet — the manufacturer block usually rides the scan response, so most
callbacks carry none and one of them erased the value for good. It is carried
across now; fresh data still wins, because a robot that changed networks is
saying so.

And the scan asked for no duplicates, which lets iOS coalesce a peripheral into
a single callback that may never include the scan response at all. The cost is a
callback per packet, bounded by the two screens that scan and only while they
are open.

* docs(ble): the robot on hand advertises no manufacturer data

Measured on a Wireless unit on 2026-08-13, on a build that keeps the field
across sightings and scans with duplicates — so the absence is the firmware's
and not the scanner's, which the two fixes before it could not have said.

Upstream PR #1086 is merged, so `BLEAdvertisement` stays and will start
answering when the firmware arrives. Until then the recovery console prints the
raw bytes, and the next measurement costs a glance rather than a build.

The consequence for anything above: identifying a robot still costs a
connection and a read of …cdef7. Do not plan on doing it from a scan.

# App Store release orchestration

Use this skill to carry a release from an approved plan to App Store review. Keep Game Center item preparation here; keep other blocker diagnosis and review recovery in `asc-submission-health`.

## Ownership boundary

This skill owns:

- staging metadata and attaching a build;
- publishing an IPA or building locally;
- submitting a prepared version;
- assembling a multi-item review submission.

Use [the preparation section](references/multi-item-submissions.md#prepare-every-item) for Game Center item preparation or attachment blockers. Use that reference's assembly and submission sections only after the app version is staged and the multi-item lane is selected. Stop and use `asc-submission-health` for other validation blockers, a stuck submission, cancellation, or retry decisions.

## Preconditions

- Resolve `APP_ID`, the version string, `VERSION_ID` when needed, and `BUILD_ID` when a build already exists.
- Configure auth with `asc auth login` or `ASC_*` environment variables.
- Confirm the intended platform. Use `IOS` unless the app targets another platform.
- Keep canonical metadata in `./metadata` when the workflow applies metadata.
- Require a dry run before a mutating high-level command, then require `--confirm` for submission.

## Choose the release lane

| Intent | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Prepare metadata and attach an existing build without submitting | `asc release stage` |
| Submit an already prepared version | `asc review submit` |
| Upload an IPA or build locally, then optionally submit | `asc publish appstore` |
| Submit the app version with IAP, subscription, or Game Center version items | lower-level `asc review` submission commands |

Do not mix lanes after one has already created a review submission. Inspect the existing submission first and continue through the matching lower-level commands.

## Run the readiness gate

Apply this gate to a version that already has the intended build attached. For the staging lane, first complete [Stage an existing build](#stage-an-existing-build); `asc release stage` attaches the build and runs validation, after which this gate can be evaluated. Do not route an expected pre-staging "build not attached" result to `asc-submission-health`.

Validate before any submission:

```bash
asc validate --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --output table
```

Use strict mode when warnings must stop automation:

```bash
asc validate --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --strict --output table
```

Digital goods are a hard gate. If the release includes IAPs or subscriptions, stop and run the relevant product checks in `asc-submission-health`. Resume this flow only after those checks have no blocking issues and the intended product versions are prepared.

For Game Center items, complete only [Prepare every item](references/multi-item-submissions.md#prepare-every-item), then return to this flow. Do not assemble or submit the multi-item review submission during readiness.

If app validation reports a Game Center item blocker, stop and use that preparation section. If the only blocker is an unattached build in the staging lane, continue to the staging section. For every other blocker, stop the release flow and use `asc-submission-health`. Do not bury unrelated remediation inside the release run.

## Stage an existing build

Use `asc release stage` to ensure the version, apply or copy metadata, attach the selected build, and run validation without creating a review submission.

Preview metadata-driven staging:

```bash
asc release stage \
  --app "APP_ID" \
  --version "1.2.3" \
  --build "BUILD_ID" \
  --metadata-dir "./metadata/version/1.2.3" \
  --dry-run \
  --output table
```

Apply the reviewed plan:

```bash
asc release stage \
  --app "APP_ID" \
  --version "1.2.3" \
  --build "BUILD_ID" \
  --metadata-dir "./metadata/version/1.2.3" \
  --confirm
```

Use `--copy-metadata-from "1.2.2"` instead of `--metadata-dir` when carrying localization metadata forward. Add `--strict-validate` when warnings should fail the stage.

## Submit a prepared version

Use `asc review submit` after metadata, review details, availability, build processing, and product readiness are already resolved.

```bash
asc review submit --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --build "BUILD_ID" --dry-run --output table
asc review submit --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --build "BUILD_ID" --confirm
```

Use `--version-id "VERSION_ID"` instead of `--version` when the exact version ID is known. `--build` may be omitted only when the intended build is already attached and verified.

## Upload or build, then publish

Use `asc publish appstore` when the release starts from an IPA or a local Xcode project/workspace.

Preview an IPA upload and submission:

```bash
asc publish appstore \
  --app "APP_ID" \
  --ipa "./App.ipa" \
  --version "1.2.3" \
  --submit \
  --dry-run \
  --output table
```

Run it after reviewing the plan:

```bash
asc publish appstore \
  --app "APP_ID" \
  --ipa "./App.ipa" \
  --version "1.2.3" \
  --submit \
  --wait \
  --confirm
```

For local-build mode, provide `--workspace` or `--project` with `--scheme` instead of `--ipa`. Use `--metadata-dir` when the publish command should apply canonical version metadata after ensuring the version.

Omit `--submit` when the user wants upload and attachment only.

## Submit multiple review items

Read [references/multi-item-submissions.md](references/multi-item-submissions.md) when the app version must ship with versioned IAP, subscription, subscription-group, or Game Center items. Add only items the user has resolved and inspected.

## Handoff after submission

Report:

- the app, version, platform, build, and submission IDs;
- which lane ran and whether it completed;
- every mutation confirmed by the user;
- the exact command to monitor the resulting submission.

Use `asc-submission-health` for monitoring, cancellation, rejection diagnosis, or retry decisions.

## Guardrails

- Do not use removed `submit-preflight`, `submit-create`, or `release-run` shortcuts.
- Do not add `--confirm` until the dry-run plan matches the requested release.
- Do not create a second review submission when one already exists for the version.
- Do not turn a validation failure into a partial release; stop at the failing gate.
- Keep data on stdout and diagnostics on stderr when wrapping commands in automation.

description: "productbuild's CSSMERR_CSP_USER_CANCELED is an unanswered keychain dialog, not a bad certificate; authorize the key once with set-key-partition-list"

minutes at `IDEDistributionPackagingStep` and then "cancels" itself. Nothing is
wrong with the certificate; `security find-identity -v` lists it as valid the

Reachy.pkg`. Written up in `docs/release.md` under "When `-exportArchive` fails",

Готово всё, кроме витрины — там уперлось в три вещи, две из которых можно закрыть только вручную.

## Сделано

**Версия и гит** — `MARKETING_VERSION` 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 (`Apps/Project.swift:31`), коммит `93b31a6` на `main`, тег `0.2.1` запушен, GitHub Release собрался (git-cliff), CI зелёный. Номер билда — счётчик коммитов, **134**.

**README** — четыре факта после `f3ef5fb` не были отражены: фильтр/сортировка/пины в сторе, лист аудио и присутствия из вьюпорта, mute/interrupt в доке, запись движений с телефона, два новых интента-вопроса. Плюс поправил утверждение про Bluetooth: скан теперь встречался с железом (робот не шлёт manufacturer data), непроверенным остался только провижининг.

**TestFlight** — билд 134 залит на обе платформы, обработан, привязан к публичной группе, **Beta App Review: `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW`** (iOS и macOS). What to Test проставлен обоим. Нотаризованный zip (24.9 МБ) висит в GitHub Release.

**Стор, что уже сделано** — записи версии переименованы 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 (0.2.0 никогда не подавалась), метаданные запушены на IOS и MAC_OS, восемь iPhone-скринов (6.9″, 1290×2796) загружены в порядке: Live 3D → Robot → Moves → Apps+док → Discover → Conversation → State → темы. `IMG_1788` (Connect «Not connected») и `IMG_1793` (дубль Apps) не брал.

## Чего не хватает для подачи

Apple ответил на попытку submit ровно двумя пунктами:

1. **`ipadPro129` обязателен** — приложение универсальное, значит нужен набор 2048×2732 или 2064×2752. iPad-скринов нет ни одного.
2. **App Privacy не опубликован** — «You must have published answers to your app's data usages». Через публичный API это недоступно; только `asc web privacy publish` (веб-сессия Apple ID + 2FA, я её здесь поднять не могу) или вручную на appstoreconnect.apple.com.

И третье, для Mac-версии: **скриншоты `APP_DESKTOP`** (1280×800 / 1440×900 / 2560×1600 / 2880×1800) — их тоже нет.

## Вопрос

App Privacy в любом случае за вами. По скринам: есть ли под рукой iPad и снять ли Mac-скрины с собранного `Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/DeveloperID/ReachyMini.app` (робот в сети, приложение подключится)? `asc review submit` for app 6799644194 was refused on 2026-08-13 with two

- `A screenshot with type ipadPro129 is required but was not provided` — the app

  `asc validate` can only say "not verifiable via the public API"; publishing
  needs an Apple ID web session with 2FA (`asc web privacy publish`) or the web
  UI, so it cannot be done from a non-interactive agent run.

A failed submit leaves a draft review submission behind and says so; a retry
reuses it, and `asc submit cancel --id <id> --confirm` is how to drop it.

**Why:** `docs/release.md` documents metadata, TestFlight and notarization in
detail and is silent on both, so the first real submission spends a round trip
discovering them.

2560x1600, 2880x1800) screenshot sets in hand *before* starting a release, and
treat App Privacy as a human step. Bumping the version is
`versions update --version-id <id> --version <new>` on the existing
PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION record, not a second `versions create` — one editable
version at a time. See [[verify-testflight-upload]], [[asc-cli-wiring]].

The Mac Installer Distribution identity lives in its own
`~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db`, with the password beside it at
`~/.config/reachy-mini/signing/keychain.pw`. A macOS App Store `-exportArchive`
run from a non-interactive shell fails as `productbuild failed`, and only the
distribution log says why: `SignData failed: … CSSMERR_CSP_USER_CANCELED`.

**Why:** macOS put up a key-access dialog nobody answered — the run hangs ~3
minutes at `IDEDistributionCreatePKGStep` and then "cancels" itself. Nothing is
wrong with the certificate; `security find-identity -v` lists it as valid the
whole time.

**Two separate things, and only one of them persists.** The partition list is
set once and stays. The **unlock does not**: the keychain is `lock-on-sleep`
with a 21600 s timeout, so every sleep of the Mac re-locks it and the identical
failure comes back — it bit twice on 2026-08-13, once per macOS build.
So **unlock immediately before every macOS release**, not once per machine:

```bash
KC=~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db
PW="$(cat ~/.config/reachy-mini/signing/keychain.pw)"
security unlock-keychain -p "$PW" "$KC"
security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$PW" "$KC"
```

**The cheap tell, before spending eight minutes on an archive:**
`security show-keychain-info "$KC"` answers `User canceled the operation.` while
it is locked and prints the lock settings once it is not.

**Recovering costs no rebuild.** `Scripts/release-macos.sh` archives
unconditionally, so `--channel appstore` would re-archive for nothing — the
Developer ID leg runs first and has already produced and notarized the same
archive. Export straight from it instead:

```bash

  -archivePath Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-macOS.xcarchive \
  -exportOptionsPlist "$(appstore_export_options true)" \
  -exportPath Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/AppStore \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates 2>&1 | xcsift
```

`security set-keychain-settings` without `-l` would end the recurrence, but that
is the user's security policy — ask, do not change it. See
[[xcode-account-signed-out]], [[app-store-submission-gates]].

- Почему повторяется: partition list живёт вечно, разблокировка — нет. Связка `lock-on-sleep`, поэтому каждый сон Mac её запирает; сегодня поймали дважды, по разу на билд.

- Восстановление без пересборки: экспорт прямо из уже сделанного архива, потому что `--channel appstore` архивирует заново восемь минут впустую.

Разомкнулось низкоуровневой командой: `review items-list --submission` показал, что элемент внутри есть, и `review submissions-submit --id … --confirm` отправил напрямую, минуя валидацию высокого уровня.
